chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Abdullah ibn Munzir, from al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever suppresses his anger while he is able to carry it out, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.إِمْضَائِهِ: its execution or carrying it out

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for suppressing anger in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the voluntary suppression of anger to the divine bestowal of 'aman' (security/peace) and 'iman' (faith), emphasizing that restraint is an active spiritual discipline rather than mere passive endurance. This concept is deeply rooted in the Shia tradition of *akhlaq* (character refinement), where controlling one's *ghadab* (anger) is seen as a key trait of the *ulul-albab* (people of understanding). The reward of inner peace on the Day of Judgment reflects the transformation of the heart from turmoil to stability through conscious self-mastery.
